guides.title: Best Things to Do in Uptown Charlotte
guides.intro: Uptown packs most of Charlotte's museums, theaters, and major-league venues into a few walkable blocks around Trade and Tryon Streets. The Levine Center for the Arts on South Tryon groups three museums together, Discovery Place keeps kids busy on North Tryon, and parks like Romare Bearden give you green space with skyline views. The LYNX Blue Line and CityLYNX Gold Line make it easy to visit without driving. These are long-standing Uptown stops worth building a day around, whether you live in a nearby high-rise or are just visiting.
guides.summary: Uptown packs most of Charlotte's museums, theaters, and major-league venues into a few walkable blocks around Trade and Tryon Streets.

items.name: Mint Museum Uptown
items.blurb: Mint Museum Uptown is a five-story art museum in the Levine Center for the Arts on South Tryon Street. It houses collections of American, contemporary, and European art, as well as the Mint's renowned craft and design collection.

items.name: Bechtler Museum of Modern Art
items.blurb: The Bechtler Museum of Modern Art, in the Levine Center for the Arts, showcases mid-20th-century modern art from the collection of the Bechtler family. Works by artists such as Picasso, Warhol, Miró, and Giacometti are displayed in a building designed by Swiss architect Mario Botta.

items.name: Harvey B. Gantt Center for African-American Arts + Culture
items.blurb: The Harvey B. Gantt Center in Uptown presents art, history, and culture of African Americans and the African diaspora.

items.name: NASCAR Hall of Fame
items.blurb: The NASCAR Hall of Fame in Uptown celebrates the history and heroes of stock car racing. Exhibits include historic race cars, interactive simulators, a pit-stop challenge, and the Hall of Honor, which recognizes inductees.

items.name: Discovery Place Science
items.blurb: Discovery Place Science is a hands-on science museum on North Tryon Street in Uptown. Exhibits cover topics such as the human body, engineering, and the natural world, and the museum also has an immersive theater and rotating traveling exhibitions.

items.name: Romare Bearden Park
items.blurb: Romare Bearden Park is a landscaped Uptown park in Third Ward named for the Charlotte-born artist Romare Bearden. Its gardens, lawns, and water features were inspired by his work, and the park offers views of the Uptown skyline.

guides.title: Best Things to Do in South End
guides.intro: South End grew up along the rail line southwest of Uptown, and today the Charlotte Rail Trail and LYNX Blue Line tie the whole district together. You can walk from converted mills to new towers and from one restaurant cluster to the next without getting in a car. Game days at Bank of America Stadium are a short walk north, and LoSo's breweries are a quick ride south. Here are a few established spots that show what makes South End one of the city's most active neighborhoods.
guides.summary: South End grew up along the rail line southwest of Uptown, and today the Charlotte Rail Trail and LYNX Blue Line tie the whole district together.

items.name: Charlotte Rail Trail
items.blurb: The Charlotte Rail Trail is a walking and biking path that runs beside the LYNX Blue Line through South End and toward Uptown. Lined with public art, seating, and pocket parks, it connects light rail stations with restaurants, breweries, apartments, and offices.

items.name: Atherton Mill
items.blurb: Atherton Mill is a converted textile mill in South End, now home to shops, restaurants, and offices. Its brick buildings sit along the Charlotte Rail Trail, near the LYNX Blue Line's East/West Boulevard station.

items.name: The Olde Mecklenburg Brewery
items.blurb: The Olde Mecklenburg Brewery, founded in 2009, is known for German-style lagers brewed according to traditional methods. Its LoSo location includes a large biergarten with shaded seating, a restaurant serving German-inspired food, and a family-friendly atmosphere.

items.name: Bank of America Stadium
items.blurb: Bank of America Stadium in Uptown's Third Ward is home to the NFL's Carolina Panthers and Major League Soccer's Charlotte FC. The stadium also hosts college football games, concerts, and other major events.

guides.title: Best Things to Do in NoDa
guides.intro: NoDa is Charlotte's arts district, set in the old North Charlotte mill village along North Davidson Street. Galleries, murals, music venues, and breweries line the main corridors, and the LYNX Blue Line's 25th Street and 36th Street stations make it easy to visit. Nearby Optimist Park and Camp North End add food halls and adaptive-reuse spaces within a short drive or bike ride. These long-running local favorites are a good starting point for exploring the neighborhood and its surroundings.
guides.summary: NoDa is Charlotte's arts district, set in the old North Charlotte mill village along North Davidson Street.

items.name: NoDa Brewing Company
items.blurb: NoDa Brewing Company is one of Charlotte's longest-running craft breweries, known for its award-winning beers, including the hazy IPA Hop Drop 'n Roll. Its North Tryon Street taproom offers a large indoor space and outdoor seating, with food trucks on many days.

items.name: Amélie's French Bakery & Café
items.blurb: Amélie's French Bakery & Café is a Charlotte favorite known for its salted caramel brownies, pastries, and cozy, eclectic decor. The original location on North Davidson Street near NoDa is a popular spot for coffee, breakfast, and late-night treats.

items.name: Birdsong Brewing Company
items.blurb: Birdsong Brewing Company is a craft brewery in Optimist Park, known for approachable beers such as its Jalapeño Pale Ale. Its taproom on North Davidson Street has indoor and outdoor seating, regular food trucks, and community events.

items.name: Optimist Hall
items.blurb: Optimist Hall is a food hall in a restored historic textile mill in Optimist Park, just north of Uptown. It brings together a variety of local and regional food vendors, coffee, and bars, with communal seating indoors and on patios.

items.name: Camp North End
items.blurb: Camp North End is a large mixed-use district just north of Uptown, created from a former industrial complex that once housed a Ford Model T assembly plant and later military and distribution uses.

guides.title: Best Things to Do in Plaza Midwood
guides.intro: Plaza Midwood's Central Avenue corridor is known for independent restaurants, bars, vintage shops, and music venues, all within a mile or so of Uptown. The neighborhood's tree-lined streets lead to Independence Park in neighboring Elizabeth, and Optimist Hall is a short drive north. Bojangles Coliseum, on Independence Boulevard, has hosted concerts and events since 1955. Start with these established spots and then wander Central Avenue to discover the rest.
guides.summary: Plaza Midwood's Central Avenue corridor is known for independent restaurants, bars, vintage shops, and music venues, all within a mile or so of Uptown.

guides.title: Best Things to Do in Dilworth
guides.intro: Dilworth, Charlotte's first streetcar suburb, pairs historic bungalow-lined streets with easy access to some of the city's best outdoor spaces. Freedom Park and the Little Sugar Creek Greenway border the neighborhood, and the Rail Trail and South End's mill-turned-retail centers are a short walk west. Park Road Shopping Center, one of the city's oldest, is just south. These spots show why Dilworth residents spend so much time outside.
guides.summary: Dilworth, Charlotte's first streetcar suburb, pairs historic bungalow-lined streets with easy access to some of the city's best outdoor spaces.

items.blurb: Freedom Park is one of Charlotte's most popular parks, sitting between Dilworth and Myers Park along Little Sugar Creek. Its centerpiece is a pond with a loop path, surrounded by ball fields, tennis and basketball courts, playgrounds, and picnic shelters.

items.name: Little Sugar Creek Greenway
items.blurb: The Little Sugar Creek Greenway is a paved trail that follows its namesake creek from near Uptown through Midtown, Freedom Park, and south Charlotte. Restored stream banks, bridges, and public art line the route, and it links several neighborhoods and parks along the way.

guides.intro: Myers Park is known for its oak-canopied streets, and many of its best destinations are green ones. Wing Haven's walled garden sits in the middle of the neighborhood, Freedom Park and the Little Sugar Creek Greenway run along its western edge, and Queens University's campus anchors Selwyn Avenue. The Mint Museum Randolph is just east in Eastover. These are some of the most established places to visit in and around Myers Park.

Independence Park, the city's first public park, is here, as is historic American Legion Memorial Stadium. Plaza Midwood's dining is a short walk away, and the Little Sugar Creek Greenway runs along the neighborhood's southern side.

guides.intro: SouthPark is Charlotte's best-known shopping district, centered on SouthPark Mall, which opened in 1970. Phillips Place adds open-air dining across Fairview Road, and Cotswold Village Shops, one of the city's original suburban centers, is a short drive north. Quail Hollow Club, a regular PGA Tour host, is just south. These established spots make SouthPark a hub for shopping, dining, and events.
guides.summary: SouthPark is Charlotte's best-known shopping district, centered on SouthPark Mall, which opened in 1970.

items.name: SouthPark Mall

items.name: Phillips Place

The Four Mile Creek Greenway runs through the area, Ballantyne Village and nearby Rea Farms and Waverly combine dining and retail, and Carolina Place mall is a short drive west in Pineville. Colonel Francis J. Beatty Park adds lake trails to the east.
guides.summary: Ballantyne and the surrounding south Charlotte communities offer greenway trails, walkable mixed-use villages, and plenty of shopping.

guides.title: Best Things to Do in Lake Norman
guides.intro: Lake Norman is the Charlotte region's biggest playground, with more than 500 miles of shoreline spread across four counties. Jetton Park in Cornelius offers lakeside paths, Lake Norman State Park near Mooresville has beaches and trails, and Birkdale Village in Huntersville is the area's go-to spot for dining and shopping. Latta Nature Preserve, on Mountain Island Lake, adds horseback riding and trails just to the south.
guides.summary: Lake Norman is the Charlotte region's biggest playground, with more than 500 miles of shoreline spread across four counties.

items.name: Jetton Park
items.blurb: Jetton Park is a Mecklenburg County park on a peninsula in Lake Norman in Cornelius. It offers paved walking and biking paths along the shoreline, picnic shelters, tennis courts, and a small beach area.

items.name: Lake Norman State Park
items.blurb: Lake Norman State Park sits on the northern shore of Lake Norman in Iredell County, near Troutman and Mooresville. It offers a swimming beach, boat launch, campgrounds, picnic areas, and a well-known network of hiking and mountain biking trails.

items.name: Birkdale Village
